unit.title: Reliable floating-point bisection as a software component
unit.scope: A bounded introduction to floating-point behavior, error-aware stopping rules, bracket invariants, Julia implementation, and deterministic tests. It does not reproduce or claim an official MIT unit.
unit.audience: A strong algorithms student building production-oriented software-engineering habits
prerequisites: Ability to read and write small programs; Julia syntax may be learned during the unit
learning_objectives: Explain why floating-point arithmetic changes the contract of a mathematical algorithm
State and preserve a bracketing invariant for bisection
Design explicit success, failure, and stagnation outcomes
Implement a small Julia API with input validation and bounded execution
Build deterministic tests around edge cases and observable invariants
Record reproducible evidence without overstating correctness

unit_completion_requires: All deliverables named in student_safe/STUDY_TASK.md are present
The submitted Julia project runs without network access and its deterministic test suite passes in the declared environment
Implementation evidence demonstrates the required input, success, failure, iteration-limit, and floating-point-stagnation behavior
The design note identifies the maintained invariant and distinguishes residual, interval width, and representation limits
Every comprehension prompt is answered in the learner's own words with references to their implementation or test evidence
An authorized validator evaluates the submission against examiner_only/RUBRIC.md
unit_completion_is_not: Completion of the catalog's ten described problem sets
Evidence that linked external materials were retrieved or studied
completion_policy.later_expansion: Additional units require separately retrieved, provenance-recorded, availability-checked materials and their own validated work.
